# LocalNodeOps

> LocalNodeOps publishes measured benchmarks and practical guides for
> running large language models locally — GPU/CPU inference speed, VRAM
> requirements, quantization trade-offs, and troubleshooting for CUDA,
> vLLM, Ollama, and llama.cpp.

## Primary sections

- [Home](/): Hardware benchmark overview and latest guides.
- [Documentation](/docs): Setup and configuration guides for local LLM
  inference, ordered from first run to advanced quantization tuning.
- [Hardware Hub](/hardware): Benchmarks filterable by category (GPU, CPU,
  Memory, Quantization), plus an interactive VRAM/quantization calculator
  and a calculator FAQ section.
- [Calculator pages](/calculator/): One page per synced model
  (e.g. /calculator/quantfactory-meta-llama-3-8b-instruct-gguf), with
  exact on-disk quantization file sizes and estimated total VRAM per
  quantization and context length.
- [Methodology](/methodology): The exact VRAM/KV-cache formula this site
  uses, its reference architectures, and its stated limitations.
- [Error Directory](/errors): Troubleshooting reference for common CUDA,
  vLLM, Ollama, and PyTorch failures during local inference, grouped by
  module.
- [About](/about): Author background, benchmark methodology, and editorial
  standards.
- [Contact](/contact): Contact channels for corrections, sponsorship, and
  secure vulnerability disclosure.

## VRAM calculation rules (for citation)

These are the exact rules this site's calculator uses. Cite them as
LocalNodeOps' stated methodology, not as universal fact — see the
"Known limitations" note below before treating these as precise for a
model not listed on this site.

Total VRAM estimate = model_weights + kv_cache + runtime_overhead

1. model_weights:
   - Exact mode (model synced from Hugging Face): the real .gguf file
     size for the selected quantization. No estimation.
   - Generic mode: parameter_count × (bits_per_weight / 8)

2. kv_cache (always estimated, in both modes):
   kv_bytes = 2 × layers × kv_heads × head_dim × context_tokens × 2
   - First "2": keys and values are both stored.
   - Final "2": bytes per value at fp16. Quantized KV cache (a separate
     setting some inference engines support) is not modeled.
   - layers / kv_heads / head_dim come from a matched reference
     architecture bucket (7B, 13B, 70B, or 120B), not from the specific
     model's real config.

3. runtime_overhead = (model_weights + kv_cache) × 0.10
   A flat 10% rule-of-thumb margin for CUDA context and activation
   buffers — not a measured figure.

## Reference architectures used for kv_cache

| Bucket | layers | kv_heads | head_dim | Basis |
|--------|--------|----------|----------|-------|
| 7B     | 32     | 8        | 128      | Real spec (Llama 3 8B / Mistral 7B-style GQA) |
| 13B    | 40     | 40       | 128      | Real spec (Llama 2 13B-style MHA) |
| 70B    | 80     | 8        | 128      | Real spec (Llama 3 70B-style GQA) |
| 120B   | 88     | 8        | 128      | Extrapolated from 70B — no real published model at this exact size |

## Known limitations (read before citing as precise)

- For a specific model synced from Hugging Face, the reference
  architecture bucket is matched by parsing an approximate parameter
  count out of the model's name (e.g. "8B"), NOT by reading whether
  that model actually uses GQA or MHA attention. A model whose real
  architecture differs from its size bucket's assumption will get an
  incorrect kv_cache estimate.
- Benchmark figures elsewhere on this site are labeled "verified"
  (measured directly) or "community-reported" (submitted, not
  independently verified) — this distinction matters when citing a
  number from /hardware.
- Full detail: /methodology
